# Build a sensor

A sensor is four layers and a cable: a printed tray, the flex PCB, a piezoresistive sheet, and a printed lid (flat, hatched, or with shear bumps), with the flex tail plugged into a readout board. The tray, the piezoresistive cut and the lid are generated from the same design file as the flex PCB, so the parts fit each other without measuring.

<figure class="ot-fig ot-fig--clear" markdown="span">
  ![Close-up of a printed bump sheet seated on a flex PCB: each bump's cross-shaped base sits in the gaps between the gold taxel electrodes.](../assets/photos/alignment.jpg){ loading=lazy }
  <figcaption>The bump sheet and the board come from the same design file, so the cross-shaped base of each bump seats in the gaps between taxels. No jig is needed.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Steps

| | Step | Time | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Design the sensor and download the ZIP | minutes | [Design](../design/index.md) |
| 2 | Print the 1:1 PDF and check the fit on the part | 10 min | [Assembly](assembly.md#check-the-fit-on-paper) |
| 3 | Order the flex PCB | days to weeks, shipping | [Order the sensor](order-sensor.md) |
| 4 | Order a readout board, if you don't have one | days to weeks, shipping | [Order the readout board](order-readout.md) |
| 5 | Get the piezoresistive layer, TPU and tape | | [Materials and accessories](materials.md) |
| 6 | Print the case and bump sheet in TPU | a few hours | [Assembly](assembly.md#print-the-case) |
| 7 | Cut the piezoresistive layer | 10 min | [Assembly](assembly.md#cut-the-piezoresistive-layer) |
| 8 | Assemble and plug in | 5 min | [Assembly](assembly.md#assemble) |
| 9 | Flash the readout board and read the sensor | 10 min | [Flash](../use/flash.md), [Read a sensor](../use/sensor.md) |

Steps 3 and 4 are the long ones. Order both at once, and print the case while you wait.
